sections.title: One sentence
sections.body: Something presented as true that still needs supporting evidence.

sections.title: In plain language
sections.body: “Our tool is faster” is a claim; a measured comparison would be evidence.

sections.title: Concrete example
sections.body: A model may suggest that Joule Studio belongs to a particular ecosystem; a reviewer must inspect the source.

sections.title: In this Knowledge OS
sections.body: Claim is educational vocabulary here, not an additional canonical database object. Proposed statements use the existing Proposal/Assertion path.

sections.title: Why it exists
sections.body: The word helps distinguish a candidate statement from accepted knowledge.

sections.title: Technical detail
sections.body: Verification claims such as F1 concern implementation correctness; they are not domain assertions.

sections.title: Implementation
sections.body: Open the checked implementation, tests, contracts and migrations below. These links identify evidence, not new verification.
